chunks: When the relatives converge, the one who is closer (in kinship) has a greater right to the inheritance of his close relative. If they are equal (in closeness), each one of them takes the place of his close relative.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: More deserving, having a greater legal right
key_terms.اسْتَوَتْ: They are equal — referring to equal degree of kinship
key_terms.السَّابِقُ: The one who precedes, i.e., the closer relative in degree of kinship
key_terms.الْقَرَابَاتُ: Relatives, kinship groups — all who are connected by blood to the deceased
key_terms.مَقَامَ قَرِيبِهِ: The place/station of his close relative — i.e., each takes the role of his nearest branch
key_terms.مِيرَاثٌ: Inheritance, the estate left by the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the rule in Shia Islam when relatives of equal closeness compete for an inheritance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a foundational principle of Islamic inheritance law: when multiple relatives compete for an inheritance, the one with a closer degree of kinship takes precedence. If two or more heirs share the same degree of closeness to the deceased, each steps into the position of his respective branch of the family for the purpose of distributing shares. This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that proximity in lineage determines priority in inheritance.

en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from a man who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When relations overlay each other then the earliest is more deserving of legacy of his relative, and if they are equal then each one takes the place of one who is close to him.’”
